source_acquisition.search_note: The PDF links to a Hugging Face checkpoint, not a code repository. gh title/method search found kamanphoebe/moe-surpass-dense.github.io with a matching paper-page description, but its master tree is an unfilled Academic Project Page template: index.html remains generic/Lorem ipsum and static carousel images/videos/sample.pdf are not this paper’s figures or tables. gh and unicli scholar found no verified plotting, table, LaTeX, notebook, SVG, or data-generation source; paper-list/reading-list mirrors were excluded. The local corpus/visual_sources/iclr-2026-a9967117d305 directory is absent. All visual properties therefore use the 22-page PDF and its 200 dpi render/PDF objects.

paper_style.palette_strategy: Object-local chart palettes: blue/teal/coral/green/yellow/purple for MoE and resource conditions, marker size for data tokens, and pale green row fill for validation-BPC minima. Plot backgrounds are light gray-purple with white grids; tables remain mostly black/gray booktabs. Color, marker, line style, and labels provide partial redundancy, but multi-series plots are not fully grayscale-safe.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: All five Figures are predominantly vector charts; pdfimages reports no raster image entries, while plot fonts appear as DejaVu Sans/Liberation Sans Type 3. Tables are vector text and rules. The only repository assets found are generic project-page template images/videos, not this paper’s charts or table generators.
paper_style.style_consistency: The ICLR two-column Letter layout, Nimbus/Times-like prose, Computer Modern mathematics, light chart background, and horizontal-rule tables are consistent. Plot text uses a DejaVu/Liberation Sans substyle; appendix tables progressively reduce size and increase variable density. Green best-row highlighting is stable across fixed-resource/reuse tables, while caption completeness varies.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1: Performance of N ≈ 2B models trained with varying data sizes D and activation rates r_a. (a) With a fixed D, performance gain exhibits a non-linear dependence on training budget C. Conversely, with a fixed r_a, increasing D leads to a linear performance gain. These findings indicate an optimal activation rate, r_a** = 20%, that is consistent across various D values when N is constant. (b) With a fixed training compute C, the optimal activation rate r_a** = 20% can be clearly seen.

color.semantic_mapping: Line color/linestyle separates fixed D and fixed r_a MoE series; marker size encodes Data~tokens; black/red horizontal lines are dense references.

plot_grammar.legend_placement: upper-right in each panel plus lower-right data-size key

encodings.x: Panel (a): total training compute C; panel (b): activation rate r_a.
encodings.color: Green/cyan/coral/magenta/yellow/blue series identify r_a or resource condition.
encodings.shape: Circular marker and size encode data-token amount.
encodings.line: Solid, dashed, dash-dot and horizontal reference lines encode fixed-D, fixed-r_a, MoE/dense conditions.
encodings.text: Axes, panel labels, legend entries and Data~tokens key.

figures.data_and_statistics: Panel (a) combines a green fixed-D=114B curve with dashed fixed-r_a curves for 8.7%, 10.8%, 19%, 35%, and 51%, while marker size shows 114B–541B data-token settings. Panel (b) fixes C=9.1e20 and compares MoE points with 2B dense references at 9.1e20 FLOPs/D=65B and 1.6e21 FLOPs/D=114B. The approximately 20% minimum is a validation-BPC point estimate; no seed, repeat, denominator, interval, or error encoding is present.
figures.evidence_relation: Eq.(1)–(10) turn N/C/D/r_a into a comparable cost language; Figure 1 is the first empirical AR result, with Tables 9–10 supplying exact 2B rows and Table 13 supplying dense baselines. Figure 2 tests the same visual claim at 7B and Figure 3 tests downstream transfer.
design_strengths: Two complementary resource views make the fixed-D versus fixed-C distinction visible.
Data-token marker size exposes the data-demand trade-off rather than hiding it.
Dense references and panel captions make the 20% claim easy to locate.
design_weaknesses: Many series and two legends compete with the small plotting area.
Log compute, resource conditions, and data-size bubbles require legend lookup.
Single validation curves have no uncertainty or independent architecture-selection holdout.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use paired fixed-data/fixed-compute panels with shared BPC grammar, explicit dense reference lines, and marker-size encoding for data budget.

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: Figure 2: Performance of N ≈ 7B models trained with varying data sizes D and activation rate r_a. The optimal activation rate, r_a** = 20%, align with the findings for the 2B models (Figure 1). Additionally, compared to training on the unique dataset, the strict data reuse scheme shows only a slight performance reduction, while the loose scheme often yields better performance.

color.semantic_mapping: Green fixed-D series is used in panel (a); blue/teal/red series in panel (b) distinguish unique, strict-reuse, loose-reuse, and dense conditions.

plot_grammar.legend_placement: upper-right in both panels and lower-right data-size key

encodings.x: Panel (a): total compute C; panel (b): activation rate r_a.
encodings.color: Blue/teal/red/green encode unique data, strict/loose reuse, and dense reference.
encodings.line: Solid/dashed/dash-dot lines encode data-reuse condition and dense reference.
encodings.text: Legend identifies N, FLOPs, data condition, and data-token bubbles.

figures.data_and_statistics: Panel (a) is a 7B fixed-D=130B curve over r_a≈8.9%–53%. Panel (b) fixes C=2.8e21 and compares unique data, strict D̂=68B, loose D=0.5D, and a 7B dense 5.4e21 FLOPs/D=130B reference; bubble sizes list 130B–608B. The minimum is BPC=0.4543 at r_a=20.07% in the corresponding fixed-C table, without seed-level uncertainty.
figures.evidence_relation: Figure 1 establishes 2B AR behavior; Figure 2 transfers it to 7B and introduces reuse curves. Tables 11–12 give 6.52B fixed-D/fixed-C rows, Table 14 gives D̂=68B reuse, and Figure 5/Table 17 cover 3B/loose reuse.
design_strengths: Same two-panel grammar makes scale consistency easy to compare with Figure 1.
Reuse schemes are visible as distinct line styles rather than a prose-only caveat.
Data-token bubbles keep the resource trade-off attached to the performance curves.
design_weaknesses: The right panel has multiple conditions and a second legend in a small area.
Strict and loose protocols are not fully defined by the caption.
Point estimates do not establish the width or stability of the optimal region.
figures.reusable_pattern: Reuse the fixed-D/fixed-C panel pair across model scales and add unique/strict/loose lines with explicit subset and epoch metadata.

figures.label: Figure 3

caption.text: Figure 3: Downstream performance of 7B models: pre-trained (top) and SFT-ed (middle and bottom) versions. Across all benchmark types, MoE models with r_a = 20% outperform dense model trained with twice the compute, aligning with upstream observations that the optimal AR is 20%.

color.semantic_mapping: Blue solid is 7B MoE unique data, teal dashed is strict reuse D̂=68B, and coral dash-dot is dense unique data D=130B; panel titles encode benchmark family and row position encodes PT/SFT.

plot_grammar.legend_placement: right of grid, with Data~tokens key above/below

encodings.shape: Circular markers; size legend additionally encodes data tokens.
encodings.facet: 3×3 benchmark-family grid; top is PT and middle/bottom are SFT.
encodings.text: Panel titles and right-side legends label benchmark family, phase, data, and model condition.

figures.data_and_statistics: Nine accuracy-vs-activation-rate panels cover Average, Knowledge, Reasoning, Comprehensive, Math, and Code across pre-trained and SFT-ed versions. Each condition has roughly six AR points; data-token bubbles range approximately 221B–511B. Caption claims r_a=20% beats a twice-compute dense model across benchmark types, while Table 2 shows task-level reversals. No seed, per-task denominator, error bar, or interval is shown.
figures.evidence_relation: Figure 1/2 upstream BPC curves motivate the AR transfer; Figure 3 is the downstream aggregate view and Table 2 restores 16 SFT benchmark rows. Appendix D enumerates 29 benchmarks and §7 explains low/high-AR and reuse exceptions.
design_strengths: Nine facets reuse one x variable, making cross-domain AR behavior immediately scannable.
A common three-series legend distinguishes unique, strict-reuse, and dense conditions.
The panel grid preserves both average headline and domain-specific behavior.
design_weaknesses: Small panels and two legends reduce label/point readability.
Category averages can conceal the benchmark-level reversals shown in Table 2.
No denominator, repeats, uncertainty, or explicit dense twice-compute line key beyond legend.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a shared AR axis across training phase and benchmark facets, then pair aggregate trends with a full per-benchmark table.

figures.label: Figure 4

caption.text: Figure 4: Results for model shape ratios ζ and μ. An overall upward trend is observed in ζ as D_m increases, while μ exhibits a downward trend with increasing D_m.

color.semantic_mapping: Color identifies D_m values 640–1536; panel x variable identifies ζ or μ and line/marker trajectories show loss observations.

encodings.x: ζ in left panel or μ in right panel.
encodings.facet: Two panels for ζ and μ.

figures.data_and_statistics: Shape-ratio sweeps plot loss for D_m=640, 768, 896, 1024, 1152, 1408, and 1536. The paper observes an overall upward ζ trend and downward μ trend, despite visibly non-monotone points. No fit, repeat, selection holdout, or uncertainty is displayed.
figures.evidence_relation: Eq.(1)–(10) define ζ/μ in the parameterization; Figure 4 and Table 8 support the §4 choice ζ≈88, μ≈22, which is then held in Tables 9–17 and Figures 1–3.
design_strengths: A shared legend and two panels compare related shape ratios without changing grammar.
The narrow loss range makes small configuration differences visible.
The plot exposes fluctuations rather than presenting the trend as perfectly monotone.
design_weaknesses: Seven colored trajectories are hard to distinguish in grayscale.
Overall trend language is stronger than a formal fit or uncertainty assessment.
No criterion explains which point becomes the production setting.
figures.reusable_pattern: Pair a shape-ratio trend plot with an exact structural table and state the selection rule separately.

figures.label: Figure 5

caption.text: Figure 5: Performance of N ≈ 3B models trained with varying data sizes D and activation rate r_a. The optimal activation rate, r_a** = 20%, aligns with the findings for the 2B models (Figure 1). Additionally, compared to training on the unique dataset, the data reuse scheme shows only a slight performance reduction. To save computational costs, only one model trained on unique data is included for reference.

color.semantic_mapping: Teal dashed/dash-dot lines are D̂=65B and D̂=114B reuse; blue solid is the unique-data reference; black/red are dense 1.4e21/2.8e21 FLOPs references.

plot_grammar.legend_placement: upper-right series key and lower/right Data~tokens key

encodings.shape: Circular markers and marker size for Data~tokens.
encodings.text: Series legend and data-token bubble legend.

figures.data_and_statistics: 3B models are compared at fixed C≈1.4e21 with D̂=65B, D̂=114B, one unique-data reference, and dense 1.4e21/2.8e21 references. The minimum is around r_a=18.83% (reported as approximately 20%) with BPC 0.4757 or 0.4747 in Tables 15–16. No seed, repeat, denominator, or uncertainty is shown.
figures.evidence_relation: Figure 5 extends the 2B/7B AR consistency claim and connects directly to Tables 15–16; it is the visual counterpart of the §6 discussion that larger unique-token budgets help under strict reuse.
design_strengths: Replicates the AR/BPC grammar at a third model scale.
Explicit dense lines and two reuse budgets make the data trade-off visible.
Caption honestly notes that only one unique-data reference was retained for cost.
design_weaknesses: One unique reference cannot establish a distribution or robust comparison.
Five series plus two legends are dense.
The exact minimum and epoch/unique-token interpretation remain table/text dependent.
figures.reusable_pattern: Reuse the same AR/BPC visual across scales, annotate the number of unique-data references, and place exact reuse settings beside it.

tables.label: Table 1

caption.text: Table 1: Notation.

tables.uncertainty: No performance statistic or uncertainty; this is a symbol dictionary.
tables.data_and_statistics: Two parallel Symbol/Definition blocks define D, M, C, N, N_a, r_a, L_e, L_d, L, α, ζ, γ on the left and S, H, D_m, D_ffn, D_h, D_e, D_se, E, K, β, μ on the right. Long definitions wrap, with no decimal precision or data rows.
tables.evidence_relation: The notation table precedes Eq.(1)–(10), Figure 1–2 axes, and every appendix configuration table; it is the interface between the fixed-resource question and the visual results.
design_strengths: Centralizes all variables used by formulas and table headers.
Parallel blocks keep a large symbol set within one page-width object.
Definitions are readable in grayscale and do not depend on color.
design_weaknesses: Caption gives no hint that two blocks serve different variable families.
Math italic and wrapped definitions are small at two-column reading scale.
No explicit link from each symbol to its first figure/table use.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use paired notation blocks with one symbol per row before introducing parameterized resource plots.

tables.label: Table 2

caption.text: Table 2: Accuracy of 7B SFT-ed models across different benchmarks.

tables.uncertainty: No standard error, interval, seed aggregation, sample denominator, or failure count.
tables.data_and_statistics: Three condition columns compare a dense baseline with MoE optimal-AR unique data and strict reuse; three metadata rows state activation rate, compute, and data-reuse condition. Sixteen benchmark rows are grouped into Knowledge (4), Reasoning (3), Comprehensive (2), Math (2), and Code (5). Accuracy is shown as two-decimal point estimates.
tables.evidence_relation: Figure 3 summarizes these downstream categories; Table 2 restores task-level reversals and connects AR20 claims to §7 discussion of strict reuse, math/code gaps, and dense exceptions.
design_strengths: Metadata rows put N/C/data conditions on the same decision surface as accuracy.
Five category groups preserve domain heterogeneity.
Bold cells make local best values easy to locate.
design_weaknesses: Caption is title-only and cannot define the three columns or bold rule.
Different benchmark scales and sample sizes are not disclosed.
Point estimates can obscure the strict-reuse regressions highlighted in prose.
tables.reusable_pattern: Follow aggregate multi-panel curves with a grouped per-benchmark table that repeats the resource conditions in metadata rows.

tables.label: Table 3

caption.text: Table 3: Pretraining data recipe compared with the LLaMA-1 recipe.

tables.uncertainty: No sample counts, deduplication rate, quality distribution, or uncertainty.
tables.data_and_statistics: Six dataset classes (WebData-en, Code, Wikipedia, Book, arXiv, StackExchange) compare Our Recipe, Our Data Set Detail, LLaMA-1 Recipe, LLaMA-1 Data Set Detail, and Recipe Diff. Percentages have two decimals and differences are signed percentage points.
tables.evidence_relation: §3.4 describes an internal high-quality corpus; Table 3 makes its mixture reproducible and provides the data recipe underlying Figure 1–5 and fixed D/N comparisons.
design_strengths: Recipe percentages and source descriptions align in one table.
The diff column exposes departures from LLaMA-1 rather than hiding them.
Wide table remains grayscale readable.
design_weaknesses: Long detail columns compress the text.
Caption does not define percentage-difference convention or data filtering.
No unique-token quality or contamination evidence is included.
tables.reusable_pattern: Compare a new pretraining mixture to a recognizable baseline with percentage, source detail, and signed difference columns.

tables.label: Table 4

caption.text: Table 4: Common training recipe.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty; settings are shared metadata rather than estimated outcomes.
tables.data_and_statistics: Two columns Hyperparameter/Setting list Vocab 65536, Adam, weight decay 0.1, gradient clipping norm 1.0, Cosine LR scheduler, warmup `clip(0.01 · Iters, 200, 2000)`, and Min LR 1e-5.
tables.evidence_relation: Table 4 is the common recipe referenced by Tables 5–17 and §3.4; it contextualizes all BPC curves without adding a new result.
design_strengths: Very short table makes shared settings easy to find.
Uses the same horizontal-rule vocabulary as other tables.
Exact warmup expression is retained.
design_weaknesses: Caption omits hardware, batch, seed, tokenizer details, and data preprocessing.
No link from each shared parameter to the experiments that vary it.
tables.reusable_pattern: Centralize shared optimizer/scheduler settings and leave experiment-specific variables to each result table.

tables.label: Table 5
tables.module: Appendix E / layer arrangement and shared expert

caption.text: Table 5: Experimental settings and results of MoE layer arrangement and shared expert. Hyperparameters shared by all experiments: D_m = 1408, D_ffn = 3904, Norm = True.

tables.uncertainty: No replicate, uncertainty, communication cost, or multiple-testing adjustment.
tables.data_and_statistics: Thirteen columns (N, N_a, M, H, D_h, L, E, K, D_e, D_se, Scheme, ℒ, Conclusion) report 10 architecture rows. Groups compare full/interleave and 1dense/1dense+SE; conclusion text says interleave performs better than full, 1dense+SE performs best, and D_se ratio impacts little.
tables.evidence_relation: §4 architecture search uses Table 5 to select 1dense+SE and D_se=KD_e before the AR sweeps in Figures 1–3 and Tables 9–17.
design_strengths: Structure, loss, and textual conclusion are co-located.
Group separators reveal the sequence of architecture decisions.
Shared-parameter caption narrows interpretation.
design_weaknesses: Thirteen dense math columns are difficult to read.
Rows change N/M and other factors, so not every contrast is isolated.
Conclusion column is qualitative and no uncertainty accompanies loss.
tables.reusable_pattern: Show architecture factors, resulting loss, and a short decision conclusion in one grouped ablation table.

tables.label: Table 6

caption.text: Table 6: Experimental settings and results of gate score normalization. Hyperparameters shared by all experiments: Scheme = 1dense, L = 17, D_m = 1408, D_ffn = 3904, H = 22, D_h = 64.

tables.uncertainty: No replicate or uncertainty; balance loss and performance are single configuration values.
tables.data_and_statistics: Eleven columns compare N, N_a, r_a, M, E, K, D_e, D_se, Norm, ℒ, and L̄_balance for four Y/N normalization rows in two expert settings. Lower balance-loss values receive local bold emphasis.
tables.evidence_relation: Appendix A equations (11)–(18) define routing and balancing; Table 6 supports §4’s decision not to normalize when K=1, before the main AR comparisons.
design_strengths: Includes both performance loss and balancing objective.
Y/N pairs isolate normalization within each expert setting.
Caption records shared architecture parameters.
design_weaknesses: Only four rows and no repeat statistic.
The K=1 zero-gradient rationale is absent from caption.
Tiny columns limit visual comparison of small differences.
tables.reusable_pattern: Pair the primary objective with the auxiliary balance objective when evaluating a router normalization choice.

tables.label: Table 7

caption.text: Table 7: Experimental settings and results of top-K setting. Hyperparameters shared by all experiments: Scheme = 1dense, L = 16, D_m = 1408, D_ffn = 3904, H = 11, D_h = 128, Norm = False.

tables.data_and_statistics: Nine columns report N, N_a, r_a, M, E, K, D_e, D_se, and ℒ for six rows, paired across K=1/11, K=2/22, and K=3/33 granularity settings. Loss has four decimal places.
tables.evidence_relation: §4 top-K discussion references Table 7 to avoid large K and K=1; the selected granularity feeds the fixed backbone used in Figures 1–5.
design_strengths: Explicitly exposes K·D_e/expert-width trade-off.
Three paired groups make the intended granularity contrasts visible.
Shared-parameter caption limits overinterpretation.
design_weaknesses: K·D_e is not strictly constant due to compatibility, weakening isolation.
No routing load or memory/communication cost.
Small single-column table requires正文 for the conclusion.
tables.reusable_pattern: Keep top-K, expert width, activated parameters, and loss together, and state any compatibility-driven mismatch.

tables.label: Table 8

caption.text: Table 8: Experimental settings and results of model shape ratios. Hyperparameters shared by all experiments: Scheme = 1dense, S = 16384, D_h = 128.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty, search criterion, or holdout; loss values are single points.
tables.data_and_statistics: Thirteen columns report N, N_a, D_m, D_ffn, L, H, E, K, D_e, D_se, μ, ζ, and ℒ for 20 structural candidates. D_m blocks range from 640 to 1920; loss is shown to three decimals.
tables.evidence_relation: Figure 4 summarizes the ζ/μ trends; Table 8 provides exact candidate rows used by §4 to set ζ≈88 and μ≈22 for later AR/reuse tables.
design_strengths: Full structure columns make the shape sweep auditable.
D_m grouping shows the intended scale progression.
Loss remains aligned with the variables used by Figure 4.
design_weaknesses: Thirteen columns and 20 rows are extremely dense.
No row is highlighted as the chosen configuration.
Non-monotone points are not accompanied by repeat/error information.
tables.reusable_pattern: Combine a shape-ratio trend plot with a complete candidate table, then state the chosen operating point in prose.

tables.label: Table 9

caption.text: Table 9: Experimental settings and results of optimal ARs for MoE models with N = 2.15B and fixed r_a. Hyperparameters shared by all experiments: L = 16, S = 2048, D_m = 1408, D_ffn = 3904, H = 11, D_h = 128, ζ = 88.

tables.uncertainty: No seed, repeat, uncertainty, or per-group variance.
tables.data_and_statistics: Fourteen columns list N_a, r_a, M, D, C, D/N, E, K, D_e, D_se, η, B, # Iters, and BPC. Eighteen rows are grouped by five fixed activation rates (8.74, 10.81, 19.11, 34.95, 50.79); BPC uses four decimals.
tables.evidence_relation: Figure 1’s fixed-D/fixed-r_a curves are backed by Table 9’s exact D/C/iteration rows; Table 10 reorganizes the same 2B configurations under fixed C and Table 13 supplies dense references.
design_strengths: Makes the compute/data denominator for each curve point explicit.
Group rules preserve fixed-r_a comparisons.
Optimizer and architecture settings are included rather than hidden.
design_weaknesses: Very wide table requires manual row aggregation.
No highlight identifies the optimal region.
Single checkpoint values cannot establish a stable region statistically.
tables.reusable_pattern: Attach every plotted fixed-factor point to a row containing consumed compute, data, architecture, and training iterations.

tables.label: Table 10

caption.text: Table 10: Experimental settings and results of optimal ARs for MoE models N = 2.15B with fixed C. Hyperparameters shared by all experiments: L = 16, S = 2048, D_m = 1408, D_ffn = 3904, H = 11, D_h = 128, ζ = 88. The green row corresponds to the MoE model with the lowest BPC on the validation set.

tables.uncertainty: Green identifies one validation minimum, not a confidence interval, replicate aggregate, or significance result.
tables.data_and_statistics: Fifteen columns list N_a, r_a, M, D, C, D/N, μ, E, K, D_e, D_se, η, B, # Iters, and BPC for 12 fixed-C AR rows from 8.74% to 57.73%. The 19.94% row is pale green with BPC 0.4857 in bold; values mix scientific notation and four-decimal BPC.
tables.evidence_relation: Figure 1b is the visual fixed-C result; Table 10 gives its exact minimum and resource row, which is compared with dense C1/C2 in Table 13 and scaled to Figure 2.
design_strengths: Fixed C is explicit in every row and caption.
Green row provides a fast selection cue.
Full resource columns allow the 0.0064/0.0049 dense differences to be reconstructed.
design_weaknesses: Fifteen columns are very small.
Single validation minimum does not quantify region width or stability.
Green-cell semantics are local and not a global statistical encoding.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a fixed-resource sweep with exact rows and a caption-defined best-row highlight, while keeping uncertainty separate from the highlight.

tables.label: Table 11

caption.text: Table 11: Experimental settings and results of optimal ARs for MoE models with N = 6.52B with fixed D. Hyperparameters shared by all experiments: L = 24, S = 2048, D_m = 2048, D_ffn = 5464, H = 16, D_h = 128, ζ = 85.3.

tables.data_and_statistics: Fourteen columns report N_a, r_a, M, D, C, D/N, E, K, D_e, D_se, η, B, # Iters, and BPC for six 6.52B rows at fixed D=130B. BPC is four decimals and no best row is colored.
tables.evidence_relation: Figure 2a’s fixed-D curve is backed by Table 11; Table 12 changes the conditioning to fixed C and Table 13 supplies 7B dense reference values.
design_strengths: Exact 6.52B resource and structure context accompanies every AR point.
Compact six-row group gives a scale-specific check.
Caption declares all shared hyperparameters.
design_weaknesses: No highlight or uncertainty makes the optimal comparison less immediate.
Wide header and scientific values are hard to scan.
Only one D budget is represented.
tables.reusable_pattern: Mirror fixed-D configuration tables across scale so the same plotted quantity remains auditable.

tables.label: Table 12

caption.text: Table 12: Experimental settings and results of optimal ARs for MoE models with N = 6.52B with fixed C. Hyperparameters shared by all experiments: L = 24, S = 2048, D_m = 2048, D_ffn = 5464, H = 16, D_h = 128, ζ = 85.3. The green row corresponds to the MoE model with the lowest BPC on the validation set.

tables.uncertainty: Green row marks a validation minimum only; no seed/interval/repeat is given.
tables.data_and_statistics: Fifteen columns list fixed-C 6.52B configurations across eight AR rows from 8.97% to 53.38%. The r_a=20.07% row is pale green and BPC=0.4543 is bold; C=2.86e21 is shared.
tables.evidence_relation: Figure 2b’s AR20 point is the Table 12 green row; Table 11 gives fixed-D context, Table 13 gives dense 7B baselines, and Figure 3 tests downstream consequences.
design_strengths: Directly exposes the scale-consistency minimum.
Caption defines the green-row semantics and shared setup.
Same columns as Table 10 support 2B↔7B comparison.
design_weaknesses: The full table is too wide for comfortable row-wise reading.
No uncertainty or region-level aggregation.
Caption does not restate the dense comparator that motivates the fixed-C choice.
tables.reusable_pattern: Repeat the fixed-C table schema at each model scale and highlight the validation minimum without presenting it as statistical certainty.

tables.label: Table 13

caption.text: Table 13: Experimental settings and results of optimal ARs for 2B, 3B, and 7B dense baselines.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty, seed aggregation, MFU, latency, or failure count.
tables.data_and_statistics: Thirteen columns report N, M, D, C, D/N, L, H, D_m, D_ffn, η, B, # Iters, and BPC for two 2B, two 3B, and two 7B dense rows. Horizontal rules separate model-size groups; BPC has four decimals.
tables.evidence_relation: Dense reference lines in Figures 1–2 and Figure 5 are grounded in these rows. Table 13 enables the 2B 0.0064/0.0049 comparison and 7B twice-compute discussion.
design_strengths: Makes N/C/D denominators explicit for every dense comparator.
Group separators match the scale logic of the figures.
Includes training parameters needed to reproduce BPC values.
design_weaknesses: Caption does not label C1/C2 or unique-data roles.
Rows mix scale and resource factors, complicating direct visual comparison.
No deployment-memory/throughput measurement despite the motivation.

tables.label: Table 14

caption.text: Table 14: Experimental settings and results of data reusing (D̂ = 68B) for MoE models with N = 6.52B with fixed C. Hyperparameters shared by all experiments: L = 24, S = 2048, D_m = 2048, D_ffn = 5464, H = 16, D_h = 128, ζ = 85.3. The green row corresponds to the MoE model with the lowest BPC on the validation set.

tables.uncertainty: Green row is the validation minimum, not a repeat-based estimate; no uncertainty or unique-data baseline error is shown.
tables.data_and_statistics: A 15-field table reports N_a, r_a, M, D, Epoch, D/N, μ, E, K, D_e, D_se, η, B, # Iters, and BPC for six 7B reuse rows at fixed C=2.86e21 and D̂=68B. r_a=20.07% is green with BPC=0.4590.
tables.evidence_relation: Figure 2b’s strict/unique comparison is expanded here; Table 14 quantifies consumed D versus unique D̂ and epochs, while Table 17 gives loose reuse.
design_strengths: Epoch, unique data, consumed data, compute and BPC are co-visible.
Green row connects the curve minimum to an auditable configuration.
Caption fixes scale and shared architecture.
design_weaknesses: Repeated M/D headers are compact and easy to misread.
No unique-data replicate or uncertainty supports the “slight reduction” claim.
No direct cost/throughput metric accompanies data reuse.
tables.reusable_pattern: Put unique subset size, epoch count, consumed tokens, compute, and loss in one reuse table.

tables.label: Table 15

caption.text: Table 15: Experimental settings and results of strict data reuse (D̂ = 65B) for MoE models with N = 3.29B with fixed C. Hyperparameters shared by all experiments: L = 24, S = 2048, D_m = 1408, D_ffn = 3904, H = 11, D_h = 128. The green row corresponds to the MoE model with the lowest BPC on the validation set.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty, repeats, or unique-data reference distribution.
tables.data_and_statistics: Fifteen columns report N_a, r_a, D, Epoch, M, C, D/N, E, K, D_e, D_se, η, B, # Iters, and BPC for nine 3B strict-reuse rows. The 18.83% row is green with BPC=0.4757; Epoch decreases as r_a increases.
tables.evidence_relation: Figure 5 and Table 16 compare D̂=65B against D̂=114B; Table 15 supports the §6 claim that more unique data helps even under fixed compute/reuse.
design_strengths: Explicit epoch and D̂ relation makes strict reuse concrete.
Scale and fixed-C setting are in caption.
Green row provides consistent selection cue with Tables 10/12/14.
design_weaknesses: Extremely wide and small table.
No repeat/uncertainty or full unique-data comparator.
Mixing D and epoch columns makes strict equality costly to reconstruct.
tables.reusable_pattern: Reuse the same strict-reuse columns at each scale and highlight validation minima with a caption-defined key.

tables.label: Table 16

caption.text: Table 16: Experimental settings and results of data reuse (D̂ = 114B) for MoE models with N = 3.29B with fixed C. Hyperparameters shared by all experiments: L = 24, S = 2048, D_m = 1408, D_ffn = 3904, H = 11, D_h = 128. The green row corresponds to the MoE model with the lowest BPC on the validation set.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty or repeated-run information; green is a single validation minimum.
tables.data_and_statistics: Fifteen columns repeat Table 15’s strict-reuse schema for D̂=114B and N=3.29B. Nine AR rows are shown, with r_a=18.83% green and BPC=0.4747; Epoch values are lower than in the D̂=65B table for the same consumed budget.
tables.evidence_relation: Figure 5’s larger-unique-data curve is grounded in Table 16; comparison with Table 15 isolates the unique-token-budget aspect of §6.
design_strengths: Same schema as Table 15 enables direct D̂ comparison.
Green row and exact BPC match the plotted extension.
Captions retain shared hyperparameters and fixed-C condition.
design_weaknesses: No uncertainty or independent reference at each AR.
Long headers and small numerals create high audit cost.
Differences in epoch/data budget are not visually separated from AR.
tables.reusable_pattern: Hold the schema fixed while varying unique-token budget so data reuse effects can be distinguished from plotting choices.

caption.text: Table 17: Experimental settings and results of loose data reuse for MoE models with N = 6.52B with fixed C. Hyperparameters shared by all experiments: L = 24, S = 2048, D_m = 2048, D_ffn = 5464, H = 16, D_h = 128. The green row corresponds to the MoE model with the lowest BPC on the validation set.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty, multi-epoch sweep beyond the listed rows, or unique-data replicate.
tables.data_and_statistics: Fourteen columns report N_a, r_a, D̂, M, C, D/N, E, K, D_e, D_se, η, B, # Iters, and BPC for six 7B loose-reuse rows at fixed C. The r_a=20.07% row is green with BPC=0.4549; D̂ changes with r_a under the two-epoch protocol.
tables.evidence_relation: Figure 2b’s loose green/dash-dot curve is expanded here; comparison with Table 14 tests the claim that two epochs can match unique data at some suboptimal points but not improve the key AR20 baseline.
design_strengths: D̂, compute, D/N and BPC make the loose definition inspectable.
Consistent green-row syntax links it to strict-reuse tables.
Caption fixes the two-epoch/fixed-C context through the surrounding text.
design_weaknesses: Caption does not itself define D̂=0.5D/two epochs.
Six point estimates cannot establish tolerance over more epochs.
No hardware or actual training-time cost accompanies the reuse claim.
tables.reusable_pattern: Report loose reuse with subset size and fixed consumed compute side by side, then pair it with strict-reuse rows.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Table 1 defines resource and shape notation; Figures 1–2 establish 2B/7B BPC-versus-activation-rate behavior under fixed D/C and reuse; Figure 3 transfers the pattern to downstream PT/SFT benchmark families, with Table 2 restoring task-level exceptions. Appendix Figure 4/Table 8 establish shape choices, Tables 5–7 establish the optimized backbone, Tables 9–13 reconstruct dense/MoE resource parity, Tables 14–17 test strict/loose reuse, and Figure 5 extends the AR pattern to 3B.
cross_object_system.caption_system: All 5 Figures and 17 Tables have numbered captions. Figure 1–5 captions generally include setup and the headline AR/reuse observation; Table 1–2 captions are short, while Tables 5–17 usually include shared hyperparameters and the green-row key. No object defines seed aggregation, uncertainty, or benchmark denominators in its caption.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Table 1 uses parallel Symbol/Definition blocks; Table 2 uses condition columns and benchmark category groups; Table 3 uses recipe/detail/difference columns; Tables 5–8 and 9–17 use dense mathematical setting headers. Horizontal booktabs/minimal rules and no vertical rules dominate. Green row fill marks the validation minimum in Tables 10, 12, and 14–17; bold is used for local best values or selected losses.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Eq.(1)–(10) and Table 1 define N, C, D, M, N_a, and r_a; Tables 5–8 choose the backbone and shape. Figures 1–2 and Tables 9–13 test AR and dense parity; Figure 3/Table 2 test downstream transfer; Figure 5/Tables 14–17 test data reuse. Expert specialization remains a prose conjecture without a routing diagnostic figure.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Main Figures 1–2 point to Tables 9–14 and dense Table 13; Figure 3 points to Table 2 and Appendix D’s 29-benchmark list; Figure 4/Table 8 support §4 shape selection; Figure 5 points to Tables 15–16. Appendix tables hold nearly all exact N/C/D/epoch/optimizer settings needed to verify the headline curves.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: NimbusRomanNo9L/Computer Modern math are stable across prose and table captions, while DejaVu Sans/Liberation Sans are stable within chart axes and legends. The variable-heavy appendix tables preserve math fonts but reduce body size enough to make Table 5 and Tables 8–17 difficult at normal zoom.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Figures 1–3 and 5 reuse blue/teal/red conditions and data-token bubble legends; Figure 4 uses a D_m categorical palette; appendix tables reuse pale green for validation minima. There is no global legend, and dense reference colors/line styles are local semantics. Grayscale retains table structure and some line distinctions but not all chart series.

most_reusable_patterns: Figure 1 pairs fixed-D and fixed-C panels and keeps data-token marker size attached to BPC.
Figure 2 and Figure 5 reuse the same AR/BPC grammar for unique, strict, and loose data reuse across scales.
Figure 3 uses a shared x-axis matrix across training phase and benchmark family, with Table 2 recovering task-level heterogeneity.
Figure 4 plus Table 8 pair shape-ratio trends with exact candidate configurations.
Tables 10, 12, and 14–17 use caption-defined green validation-minimum rows to connect plotted minima to reproducible settings.
highest_value_objects: Figure 1 is the primary equal-resource/optimal-AR visual.
Figure 2 is the core 7B consistency and data-reuse result.
Figure 3 and Table 2 connect downstream headline trends to benchmark-level reversals.
Tables 10, 12, 13, and 14 are essential for reconstructing fixed-C/fixed-D MoE versus dense comparisons.
failure_patterns: Every Figure reports point curves without seed, replicate, or uncertainty encoding.
Figure 3 category averages hide task-level reversals that only Table 2 reveals.
Tables 5–17 are wide and small, making N/C/D/epoch fairness costly to audit.
Green best-row highlighting can be mistaken for statistical significance.
Expert specialization is proposed as a mechanism but has no routing/causal diagnostic figure; the project-page repository is a generic template rather than a visual source.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: The paper uses unified N/C/D/r_a parameterization as a visual spine, demonstrates an approximately 20% activation-rate region from 2B to 7B and 3B BPC curves, transfers it to downstream panels and per-benchmark results, and moves the full architecture, dense-baseline, and data-reuse configurations into appendix tables.
